Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: RDL can fan die connections outward within a molded package without requiring a conventional package substrate in that layer. Trace the visual in order: embedded die; RDL; external connection. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Trace a pad through RDL to an external joint in a conceptual fan-out cross-section.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Trace a pad through RDL to an external joint in a conceptual fan-out cross-section. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
